method: Individual reading of PDF pages 45–51, segments 734–850; distinguish quoted statements, allegations, narrator opinions and unresolved transcript errors. No verification of real-world case outcomes is implied.
phrases: more or less
approximately, or with roughly the same meaning
大致；差不多
That's more or less what she said.
她说的大致就是这个意思。
Signals a paraphrase, so the following imagined wording must not be presented as a verbatim university quotation.
rise to this challenge
respond successfully to a difficult situation
迎接并应对这一挑战
The team will rise to this challenge.
团队会迎接并应对这一挑战。
Formal motivational language in the quoted statement, not a claim that the challenge has already been resolved.
combing through
examining something very carefully to find information
仔细搜查；逐一查阅
We spent the morning combing through old records.
我们花了一上午仔细查阅旧记录。
Figurative combing, not grooming hair; the narrator doubts reporters were doing this.
can't help but
cannot avoid doing or thinking something
忍不住；不由得
I can't help but wonder why the date changed.
我不由得想，日期为什么改了。
Follow with the base verb; the phrase describes the narrator's reaction, not evidence of deliberate concealment.
put together
organized or assembled something from people or parts
组建；组织起来
They put together a team for the project.
他们为这个项目组建了一个团队。
Panel is an assembled group, not a physical board being constructed.
press charges
seek to have a criminal accusation formally pursued
要求追究刑事责任；提出刑事控告（通俗说法）
The article discusses whether anyone sought to press charges.
文章讨论是否有人要求追究刑事责任。
Ordinary-language expression, not a claim that a private individual controls prosecution; surrounding claims about authority remain attributed and require legal-context review.
be that as it may
despite what has just been said
尽管如此；话虽如此
The plan is expensive; be that as it may, we still need a solution.
这个方案很贵；话虽如此，我们仍然需要一个解决办法。
Concession returns to the timeline without resolving the earlier speculation about delays.
kicking up
becoming more active or intense
开始活跃起来；加剧
By noon, the wind was really kicking up.
到中午时，风明显大了起来。
Informal activity/intensity sense; source things start really kicking up is less specific than starting a formal proceeding.
drops out of school
leaves school before completing the course of study
中途退学
In the novel, the main character drops out of school to work.
小说中的主人公中途退学去工作。
Teaching example is fictional and adapted; source attributes the departure to the post-assault period without adding motives.
gets picked up
is taken up and reported by media organizations
被媒体跟进报道
The local story gets picked up by a national newspaper.
这则地方新闻被一家全国性报纸跟进报道。
News uptake, not physical lifting, collection by car or arrest.
blows up
suddenly attracts a great deal of attention
迅速引发广泛关注；爆火
The video blows up after a popular account shares it.
一个热门账号转发后，这段视频迅速引发广泛关注。
Figurative spread of attention, not an explosion or an angry outburst.
as soon as
immediately after a particular event or condition
一……就……；尽快在……之后
I'll send the file as soon as I finish editing it.
我一编辑完就把文件发给你。
Source ties the next release to finishing the edit, not a promised date or fabricated timestamp.
segments: Continuation of the prior page's name list; spellings and full list boundaries require source tracking rather than lexical matching.

Narrative now moves the account forward to January, without changing the recording's dates.

Title Nine and federal identify the law and its governmental level; the incomplete definition continues in later paragraphs.

Federal assistance means national-government support; like a billion is an approximate narrator claim, not a verified current funding figure.

Restates the investigation's narrated start month, with commences as formal begins.
Put together means assemble people, but panel needs the group-of-reviewers sense; the phrasal verb alone does not explain the role.
Narrator uses panel as shorthand for this investigation; a panel is not universally synonymous with the whole Title IX process.
No longer with describes the narrated change of institutional handling; it does not establish that all possible parallel processes ended.
Identifies the process the narrator is discussing now, without treating it as a criminal proceeding.
Simple statement of an intention to investigate what happened; no conclusion is asserted.
A lot on means much discussion about the investigation in the forthcoming account, not a physical load.
Simple institutional-subject statement introducing the speakers' subsequent criticism.
Short affirmation of the preceding statement.
Themselves is an isolated reflexive used rhetorically to allege self-investigation; its referent and scope need annotation.
Basically qualifies the agreement as a simplified characterization.
Panel means an assembled group here, and little can be dismissive; it needs a contextual teaching entry.
On there means on the panel in context; the basic statement does not verify professional qualifications beyond the narrator's claim.
Negated federal-prosecutor role distinguishes the school group from national-government criminal prosecutors.
Equipped is skills/resources rather than physical gear; might have been preserves contingency, and the competence assessment remains the narrator's opinion.
Subpoena power, search warrant and DA need precise legal-role glosses; probably marks speculation and a prosecutor card cannot validate the powers described.
Repeats the type of institutional investigation without adding a new procedural claim.
No matter what they find is a concessive fragment leading into a legal-authority claim; the sentence must be explained across the boundary.
The everyday phrase is taught, but who they refers to and the legal scope of cannot need contextual verification rather than blanket approval.
Criminally is reviewed, but take this criminally is nonstandard wording attached to a sweeping authority claim; preserve and annotate, not endorse as a legal rule.
Missing months metaphorically asks about an unexplained timeline gap; it does not mean calendar months literally disappeared.
Could be introduces alternatives, and healing/traumatized relate to recovery and distress; none of the explanations is asserted as verified.
Several hedges end in an unfinished there's clause; do not certify the fragment without its continuation.
Gap completes the previous sentence and refers to elapsed time; isolated treatment would hide the cross-paragraph syntax.
Commence is begin and the concession phrase sets aside prior uncertainty without resolving it.
Kicking up is increasing activity, not physical kicking; the source ties it to the narrated month rather than a new date.
Hearings is a procedural-event noun needing distinction from ordinary listening; the numeric claim remains attributed.
Expelled must be distinguished from suspended, and it appears qualifies the outcome; investigation vocabulary alone does not explain the sanction.
Run-on combines suspension, return timing and a question about expulsion; different penalties and speaker turns still need annotation.
Expelled versus suspended and uncertain Jillio name rendering are unresolved; do not silently normalize identities or merge sanctions.
Involved in sexual activity is reported as others' wording; the phrase can obscure allegations and requires careful attribution rather than unqualified teaching.
Brief acknowledgment with so far limiting understanding to what has been explained.

Crude quoted message ends in alum and needs register/abbreviation support; sending it remains an attributed allegation.

Conduct is a vague reference to alleged acts and the name variant Jillia remains uncertain; preserve source spellings.
Sanctions are penalties, but egregious and multiple speculative hedges require explanation; the reason for different outcomes is not established.
So why are people so is abandoned before a new question; sentence repair and expulsion terminology remain barriers.
Expelled, suspended and back are combined in a broken correction; do not assign a definite outcome to a named person from this fragment.
Explicit uncertainty about whether someone returned; no further lexical obstacle beyond the known person reference.

Simple reported sighting and recording; last week remains relative to the recording rather than the review date.
Short assertion of return in the speakers' account, not independently confirmed by this review.

Simple restatement of the reported campus sighting.

Continuation of the list of defendants; the bar name and organizational role need linkage to the preceding sentence.

phrase:10:for the rest of my life
Haunt is persistent distressing memory and the time phrase expresses feared lasting impact; it is not a prediction that recovery is impossible.
News uptake, speed and broad-audience organizations are all explained; almost every outlet remains the narrator's unverified scope claim.
Blows up means rapidly attracts attention, not a physical explosion; the described celebrity activity remains attributed to the account.
Closing transition identifies the end of this first half, not the end of the whole case.
DA's office still needs a contextual institutional gloss; go through means discuss the statements, not physically pass through an office.
The previously reviewed Unit 1 card explains bizarre as very strange; here it conveys the narrator's judgment rather than a factual case outcome.
DA role and handling it need explanation; now in 2026 belongs to the recording and the unprecedented claim is the narrator's personal judgment.
As well as adds forthcoming material to the preview; allegations remain claims and released messages are not automatically authenticated by mention.
chunk:10:that's all going to be covered
Covered means discussed in a future episode section, not this project's learning-coverage status.
Conventional closing wish for safety without an additional lexical obstacle.
The time connector is taught, but come up ambiguously refers to the next release and edit has an implicit object; no release date or timestamp may be invented.
